title: WooCommerce emails not sending? Diagnose it in four steps

linkedin.post:
Would you notice if your store stopped sending order emails today?

Most owners find out when a customer writes, "I never got my order email." Orders sit in your dashboard. Nobody hears anything. Buyers wonder if the purchase went through, and support tickets pile up.

No jargon, no guesswork. A missing email fails at one of four stages, and each stage has its own first place to look. Installing a mail tool before you know which stage broke costs days.

Here are the five things to check, in the order to check them:

1️⃣ The email never starts
Sometimes the order never reaches the point where an email fires. A payment left half finished is a common cause. The email may also be switched off, or have no one to send to. Most of these cases end with one setting or one status.

2️⃣ The store tried and failed
Your store keeps a record of every attempt. It shows whether the message went out or was skipped. Reading that record takes minutes and names the stage. Until you read it, you are guessing.

3️⃣ The inbox said no
The message left your store, but the receiving inbox refused it. A sending address on a free mail service is a common reason. Your own domain gives inboxes something to trust. Sent in your store does not mean accepted by theirs.

4️⃣ It landed in spam
The customer did check. The email was filed as junk because the inbox could not confirm it came from you. Customers rarely look there, so they assume you never sent it. Your host or mail service can confirm that proof is in place.

5️⃣ When to call a developer
Some problems need access you may not have. Paid orders that never move forward, or the same fault coming back, are signs. Hand over your test results and the record, and the fix gets shorter.

If a customer placed an order right now, could you say which stage would fail first?

Check that the order moved forward and the email is switched on.

2️⃣ The store tried and failed

3️⃣ The inbox said no
Send from an address on your own domain, not a free mail one.

4️⃣ It landed in spam
Ask your host to confirm inboxes can verify the email came from you.
